questions.stem: This echocardiogram is from a patient who uses injectable drugs. The mobile echodensity indicated on the valve most likely represents which of the following?

choices.label: D
choices.text: A bland thrombus from atrial fibrillation

choices.label: E
choices.text: A Libman-Sacks vegetation of systemic lupus erythematosus

explanation.summary: Injection drug use delivers bacteria directly into the venous blood, and the tricuspid valve is the first valve these organisms encounter, making right-sided infective endocarditis common. The echo shows a vegetation on the tricuspid valve projecting into the right ventricle, adjacent to the right atrium.

questions.stem: This diagram depicts an embolus occluding a cerebral artery. In a patient with mitral stenosis and atrial fibrillation, the embolus most commonly originates in which cardiac chamber?

explanation.summary: In mitral stenosis and atrial fibrillation, loss of organized atrial contraction causes blood to stagnate in the dilated left atrium, promoting thrombus formation. A dislodged thrombus travels through the systemic arterial circulation and the internal carotid artery to occlude a cerebral vessel, producing a cardioembolic stroke.
